title: Mabeyn to Yemen, system B: two-digit numeral cipher (values about 44-49, 55-59, 64-71) with the clerk's Arabic letters written above the numbers, nine or more telegrams 1896-1901, with same-day clear copies for 28 Apr 1901 and 5 Jun 1901
correspondents: Mabeyn-i Hümayun cipher clerks (Mehmed Kamil, Asım) -> Yemen Province (Hüseyin Hilmi Paşa)
shelfmark: Koç University, Hilmi Paşa Belgeleri Koleksiyonu (HPBK) items 587, 602, 562, 546, 577, 575, 578, 599, 576, 580, 585; clear copies 725, 748, 726, 764, 1070
folio_note: Viewed on 14 Nov 2026 (contact sheets, 576/578 at full size): 576, 578, 575, 587, 602, 562, 546, 577, 580, 585, 599. All show a numeral stream on a Télégramme form with a single Arabic letter written above most numbers, apparently the clerk's decipherment, i.e. a crib inside the ciphertext (not yet checked letter by letter). 725 (28 Apr 1901, clear: a proposal to a bandit leader) and 726 (5 Jun 1901, clear: to cipher clerk Asım on German agitation) are clear sheets of the same days as 578/599 and 576; 764 and 1070 look clear too.
status: Catalogue calls 576 "content could not be deciphered"; the letters above the numbers are not mentioned. No published decipherment found. The previous sweep (row 3) listed 576 and 578 only as undeciphered.
why: A ciphertext that carries a letter-by-letter reading above it, in a small numeral alphabet (about 20 values, homophones for frequent letters), plus clear copies of the same days, makes the key recoverable from the page and checkable against the clear copies; a dozen telegrams give a corpus.
verify: Transcribe numerals and letters for 576 and 578, tabulate number->letter, test it on 587/602/562/546/577/575/580/585/599, and compare the readings for 28 Apr 1901 and 5 Jun 1901 with 725/748 and 726; then 1070 for 6 Feb 1900 (575).
score_note: importance 3 (modest messages, new vein), solvability 5 (interlinear letters on the page), difficulty 2
